title: Harden the remaining public and signed-in write sinks: rate limits and replay windows on the CSP report, status routes, /api/track, /api/observe and the four FlowWeb webhooks, and a loud signal when Upstash is missing

source.ref: Whole-site audit 2026-11-16 (project thread, requested by Daniel). Confidence: CONFIRMED. Audit file: audit/FINAL-BUILD-AND-REPAIR-LIST-2026-11-16.md

detail:
EVIDENCE: app/api/csp-report/route.ts:13-27 calls req.json() with no size cap or limiter and logs every report; app/api/status/cron-freshness/route.ts:12 (readCronStamps) and app/api/status/queue-lag/route.ts:19 (queueHealth) hit the database on every unauthenticated, no-store GET. app/api/spotlight/click and unsubscribe are limited or token-gated, so these are the outliers. || app/api/track/route.ts:16-45 and app/api/observe/route.ts:21-70 contain no rateLimit call; observe caps a batch at 50 (lib/analytics/interaction-events.ts:17) but not batches per minute and inserts with the admin client. Every /api/v1 route is limited (37 of 37 use rateLimited). || app/api/webhooks/flowweb-crm/route.ts:21, flowweb-facts:19, flowweb-link:26, flowweb-outcomes:24 all read FLOWWEB_OUTCOMES_SECRET; lib/flowweb/claim.ts:34-40 verifySignature is HMAC over ts.body with MAX_SKEW_MS and no nonce store. Signature compare is timing-safe and fail-closed when the secret is unset (good). flowweb-claim has its own FLOWWEB_CLAIM_SECRET. || lib/rate-limit.ts:8-13 and :108 (default deny, 'allow' opt-out); rg finds whenUnconfigured: 'allow' in 23 files including sign-in (OPEN_WHEN_UNSET), spotlight click, create-space draft, vera turn. app/api/status/route.ts exposes rateLimitConfigured() so the state is observable but nothing alerts on it.

WHY IT MATTERS: Cheap amplification: a loop against these costs log volume and DB time. No data leaks (responses carry counts only). A logged-in script can bloat interaction_events and engagement tables, which skews growth reporting and costs storage. Leak of one integration's secret opens all four, and a captured request can be replayed briefly. The endpoints are mostly read-only or idempotent, so impact is small. Sign-in and AI doors are the ones most worth throttling at launch. The design is deliberate; the gap is that no gate notices if KV is absent.

FIX DIRECTION: Add rateLimitOk (whenUnconfigured: 'allow') to the three, a 10KB body cap on csp-report, and a 30s edge cache on the status reads. rateLimitOk keyed on profile id (for example 120 per minute) with whenUnconfigured: 'allow'. Give crm and link their own secrets, or bind the path into the signed string; keep idempotency on the write routes. Confirm KV_REST_API_URL/TOKEN are set in Vercel production, and add rateLimitConfigured to the queue-watch workflow so it pages when false.

2026-11-16 fixed (security thread): rateLimitOk (allow when KV is unset) on csp-report (plus a 10KB cap), both status reads, /api/track and /api/observe (per member), and all four FlowWeb webhooks (per IP). facts, link and crm now read their own FLOWWEB_FACTS_SECRET / FLOWWEB_LINK_SECRET / FLOWWEB_CRM_SECRET through lib/flowweb/secret.ts and fall back to the shared FLOWWEB_OUTCOMES_SECRET, so nothing breaks on deploy; OWNER ACTION: set the three secrets in Vercel and the sender's Keychain to retire the shared fallback. queue-watch now fails when /api/status reports rateLimit false. Not done by design: a replay nonce store (the sender may legitimately resend the same signed request inside the 5 minute window, and the routes are idempotent); the 30s edge cache on status reads (their comments say a stale answer is the failure they exist to catch, so they stay uncached and are throttled instead). Not checked: whether KV_REST_API_URL/TOKEN are set in Vercel production; the new workflow step will say.

verify.note: Fails on 2026-11-16 (audit run). Passes when the fix lands. Audit-written probes are direction checks; retime only with Daniel's phrase.
